#### 1. adenine phosphoribosyltransferase deficiency  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.476)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-74217)

**Proposed mechanism:** HPRT1 (HGNC:4869) —DISRUPTS→ Hypoxanthine (CHEBI:17447); HPRT1 (HGNC:4869) —DISRUPTS→ Guanine (CHEBI:17479); Hypoxanthine (CHEBI:17447) —LEADS_TO→ Purine Salvage Pathway (REACT:R-HSA-168922); Guanine (CHEBI:17479) —LEADS_TO→ Purine Salvage Pathway (REACT:R-HSA-168922); Purine Salvage Pathway (REACT:R-HSA-168922) —LEADS_TO→ Neurological abnormalities (HP:0000707); APRT (HGNC:483) —DISRUPTS→ Adenine (CHEBI:15356); Adenine (CHEBI:15356) —LEADS_TO→ Purine Salvage Pathway (REACT:R-HSA-168922); Purine Salvage Pathway (REACT:R-HSA-168922) —LEADS_TO→ 2,8-dihydroxyadenine (CHEBI:16599); 2,8-dihydroxyadenine (CHEBI:16599) —LEADS_TO→ Urolithiasis (HP:0000063). Mutations in HPRT1 disrupt the salvage of hypoxanthine and guanine, leading to accumulation of uric acid and neurological symptoms. Mutations in APRT disrupt the salvage of adenine, leading to the accumulation of 2,8-dihydroxyadenine, which forms kidney stones. Both pathways converge on the purine salvage pathway, highlighting a shared metabolic process despite different substrates and distinct primary clinical outcomes.

**How to falsify it:** The presence of pathogenic variants in HPRT1 or APRT with significantly different functional consequences (e.g., a gain-of-function variant in one gene while the other is loss-of-function) would falsify the shared loss-of-function mechanism. Additionally, if genetic studies reveal distinct upstream regulatory mechanisms or downstream effector pathways that are completely independent of the purine salvage pathway for each disease, this would also challenge the proposed overlap. _(variant: The identification of common, benign variants (AF > 1%) in the coding regions of HPRT1 and APRT in the general population that do not segregate with either disease would support the proposed mechanism.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared reliance on the purine salvage pathway despite distinct genetic origins can inform therapeutic strategies. For instance, interventions aimed at modulating purine metabolism or managing the downstream consequences (e.g., crystal deposition, neurotransmitter imbalances) could potentially benefit patients with either disorder.
